entries.sentence: Early chronic kidney disease usually causes no symptoms, and it is often found by chance when a blood or urine test is done for another reason.
entries.note: Summary of NHS/NHS inform: early CKD usually no symptoms, often found by chance through blood or urine test.

entries.sentence: Symptoms can appear at a more advanced stage, including tiredness, swollen ankles, feet or hands, shortness of breath, feeling sick and blood in the urine.
entries.note: Summary listed these advanced-stage symptoms (NHS).

entries.sentence: Later kidney failure can also bring itching, muscle cramps and changes in how often a person passes urine.
entries.note: Summary: late-stage kidney failure can bring itching, muscle cramps, urination changes.

entries.sentence: Doctors describe the condition in stages, and a higher stage means more severe disease.
entries.note: Summary: CKD is staged, the higher the stage the more severe.

entries.sentence: In stage 1 the filtering is normal but there is other evidence of kidney damage, and stage 2 is a slight decrease in function.
entries.note: Summary: stage 1 normal eGFR with other evidence of damage; stage 2 slight decrease. Numbers deliberately omitted.

entries.sentence: Stage 3 is split into 3a and 3b, stage 4 is a further fall, and stage 5 is known as established kidney failure.
entries.note: Summary: stage 3 split 3a/3b, stage 4, stage 5 established renal failure.

entries.sentence: Only a small proportion of people with the condition go on to kidney failure, which the NHS puts at around 2 in 100 people.
entries.note: Summary: NHS says CKD only progresses to kidney failure in around 2 in 100 people.

entries.sentence: When the kidneys do stop working, this usually happens gradually, so there is time to plan the next stage of treatment.
entries.note: Summary: usually gradual, so there should be time to plan the next stage.

entries.sentence: Chronic kidney disease can be diagnosed with blood and urine tests.
entries.note: Summary: NHS says CKD can be diagnosed with blood and urine tests.

entries.sentence: The blood test is used to estimate how well the kidneys are filtering, and the urine test looks for protein and blood.
entries.note: Summary: blood test estimates filtering; urine test checks albumin and creatinine plus blood or protein.

entries.sentence: Once the condition is diagnosed, kidney function is followed with regular blood and urine tests.
entries.note: Summary: once diagnosed, function tracked with regular blood and urine tests.

entries.sentence: Some people are tested more often, including those taking long-term medicines that can affect the kidneys, such as lithium, omeprazole or anti-inflammatory painkillers called NSAIDs.
entries.note: Summary: more frequent testing for people on long-term medicines such as lithium, omeprazole, NSAIDs.

entries.sentence: The condition commonly affects blood pressure, red blood cell counts and bone health, so these may be checked as well.
entries.note: Second search: CKD commonly affects blood pressure, red cell counts, bone health; the 'may be checked' part is inference from a summary that suggested the care team may check blood pressure, cholesterol and blood counts. Source blend uncertain.

entries.sentence: A referral to a dietitian is common, so that diet advice can fit the person.
entries.note: Second search summary said dietitian referral is common for personalised diet advice; page attribution uncertain.

entries.sentence: The NHS says most people with the condition can control it with medicine and regular check-ups.
entries.note: Summary: NHS notes most people with CKD can control their condition with medicine and regular check-ups.

entries.sentence: There is no cure for chronic kidney disease, but treatment can help relieve the symptoms and stop it getting worse.
entries.note: Summary: NHS says no cure but treatment can help relieve symptoms and stop it getting worse.

entries.sentence: The NHS describes lifestyle changes to stay as healthy as possible, together with medicines to manage problems such as high blood pressure and high cholesterol.
entries.note: Summary: NHS guidance lists lifestyle changes and medicines for blood pressure and cholesterol.

entries.sentence: ACE inhibitors are commonly used for blood pressure in this condition, and statins may be prescribed to lower the risk of heart and blood vessel problems.
entries.note: Summary: ACE inhibitors per NHS inform; statins for cardiovascular risk per NHS 111 Wales.

entries.sentence: Anaemia, a shortage of red blood cells, is common, and most people with kidney disease are given iron because it is needed to make red blood cells.
entries.note: Summary: anaemia common in CKD; most given iron since needed for red blood cell production (Renal Association/Kidney Care UK blend). Plain definition of anaemia is added gloss.

entries.sentence: Further anaemia treatment may involve a medicine called erythropoietin.
entries.note: Summary: further treatment may involve erythropoietin, per Renal Association guideline.

entries.sentence: Medicines can also be used for other symptoms of kidney failure, such as breathlessness, loss of appetite and itchy skin.
entries.note: Summary: medicines to treat breathlessness, anaemia, loss of appetite, itchy skin are part of supportive care.

entries.sentence: For a small number of people the kidneys eventually stop working, and dialysis or a transplant is then considered.
entries.note: Summary: for a small proportion kidneys eventually stop; dialysis and transplant are the main options for kidney failure.

entries.sentence: Dialysis is a way of removing waste products and extra fluid from the blood.
entries.note: Summary: dialysis removes waste products and excess fluid from blood.

entries.sentence: NIDDK describes haemodialysis as running the blood through an external filter by machine, while peritoneal dialysis uses the lining of the abdomen as the filter inside the body.
entries.note: Summary: NIDDK haemodialysis external machine filter; peritoneal uses lining of abdomen.

entries.sentence: A kidney transplant is the other main option, and the kidney can come from a living or a deceased donor.
entries.note: Summary: transplant is the other main option; NHSBT covers living and deceased donors.

entries.sentence: NHS Blood and Transplant says living donors account for roughly 30 in 100 kidney transplants, with a much shorter wait than for a kidney from a deceased donor.
entries.note: Summary: living donors roughly 30 in 100 transplants; waits much shorter (3-6 months vs 2-3 years, not repeated).

entries.sentence: People with a transplant take anti-rejection medicines for as long as the new kidney works, and NIDDK notes these can cause other health problems.
entries.note: Summary: NIDDK says anti-rejection medicines are needed as long as kidney works and may cause other health problems.

entries.sentence: Some people choose not to have dialysis or a transplant, or these may not suit them, and supportive care then aims to control symptoms with medical, psychological and practical support.
entries.note: Summary: supportive care without dialysis or transplant, with medical, psychological and practical support.

entries.sentence: The NHS says many people with the condition live long lives without being unduly affected by it.
entries.note: Summary: many people with CKD are able to live long lives without being unduly affected.

entries.sentence: Looking after general health still matters, particularly to reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke.
entries.note: Summary: general health matters, particularly to reduce heart disease and stroke risk.

entries.sentence: Lifestyle advice includes stopping smoking for those who smoke and keeping physically active.
entries.note: Summary: stop smoking among usual lifestyle measures; exercise recommended.

entries.sentence: Guidance favours plenty of fruit, vegetables and pulses, with smaller amounts of animal protein such as meat, fish and eggs.
entries.note: Summary: NHS-linked guidance favours fruit, vegetables, pulses, less animal protein. Numeric salt/exercise targets deliberately omitted.

entries.sentence: It also advises limiting salt, and diet advice from a dietitian is individual and changes as the disease progresses.
entries.note: Summary: salt restriction per NHS; individualised diet changing with progression from a second-search summary; attribution blended.

entries.sentence: Regular ibuprofen-type painkillers are best avoided because they can affect kidney function.
entries.note: Summary: avoiding regular ibuprofen-type painkillers is advised as they can affect kidney function.

entries.sentence: People are advised to check with their care team before starting a new exercise programme.
entries.note: Second search summary: regular exercise, checking with care team first; page attribution uncertain.

entries.sentence: Heart and blood vessel disease is a major concern in chronic kidney disease.
entries.note: Summary: heart problems are a major concern; most patients die of cardiovascular complications rather than progressing to kidney failure.

entries.sentence: Research summaries note that people with the condition are more likely to die of heart and blood vessel complications than to reach kidney failure.
entries.note: Same summary, paraphrased; sources were PubMed/PMC blend, so attribution to MedlinePlus is uncertain.

entries.sentence: Anaemia is widespread, and it becomes more common as kidney disease advances.
entries.note: Summary: anaemia widespread, more common in advanced disease.

entries.sentence: Bone problems can also develop, because the balance of calcium, phosphate and vitamin D in the body is disturbed.
entries.note: Summary (StatPearls/PMC blend): mineral and bone disorders with disruptions in calcium, phosphate, parathyroid hormone, vitamin D.

entries.sentence: Because of these links, treatment looks at the heart, the blood and the bones as well as the kidneys.
entries.note: Inference from the above and NHS treatment summary (medicines for blood pressure, cholesterol, anaemia, phosphate imbalance).

entries.sentence: NHS 111 Wales gives the proportion who reach kidney failure as around 1 in 50 people.
entries.note: Summary: NHS 111 Wales gives same figure as around 1 in 50.

entries.sentence: For most people the outlook depends on controlling the condition with medicine and regular check-ups.
entries.note: Paraphrase of NHS statement that most people can control CKD with medicine and regular check-ups.

entries.note: As in sections.

entries.sentence: In that case the aim of supportive care is to treat and control the symptoms of kidney failure.
entries.note: Summary of supportive care.
